ranked.name: NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 (current destination)
ranked.why:
Its verified execution-simulation building blocks are the strongest in the set. They include a FillModel with prob_fill_on_limit/prob_slippage, a LatencyModel with separate insert and update latencies, and L1-L3 matching (https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/blob/e7a6e6189c061d9a5b571d27191e90e6b59edef8/crates/execution/src/models/fill.rs ; .../latency.rs). Repo gates established on it:
- spy-lean-parity one_zero PASS: 136 checks, 0 failed
- dividend-sim-module
- native Alpaca paper fault behaviour
(catalogs/us-equities/runtime-target.json and gates-20260922.json at origin/main 9c1669c7). The corrected 2026-09-25 hftbacktest cross-check agrees with it within tolerance (blueprints/us-equities/sim-engine-crosscheck/README.md). LGPL-3.0; Rust core with Python; Linux and macOS ARM64 per https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/getting_started/installation/.

Weak points:
- No upstream Alpaca adapter. RFC #3374 has been open since 2026-01-01, and adapter PR #3375 was closed unmerged the same day; the maintainer cited project capacity (https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/pull/3375).
- Corporate-action support is still an open request (https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/issues/3307).
- rc5 is a prerelease with the IBKR stock-order blocker #4983.
ranked.versus_current: This is the current destination. Compared with LEAN, it has better fill, latency and queue modelling and native Python/Rust portability with no paid gates. It is worse on packaged equity data (no security master; corporate actions open upstream) and has no official Alpaca adapter, so the in-repo alpaca-py adapter stays load-bearing.
ranked.trial: No platform trial. Its open risk sits inside the existing protocol: extend compare.py from one_zero to the blocked one_stress, two_zero, two_stress, adaptive_stress and over_limit cases (backtesting-engine open_gaps, catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json). Pass = PASS inside tolerances.json with zero unexplained cash residue.

ranked.name: LEAN / QuantConnect + Lean.Brokerages.Alpaca + lean-cli (retained oracle; Alpaca brokerage conditional)
ranked.why:
The only engine with an official, maintained Alpaca brokerage, live-data handler and history provider (plugin head e623e796, pushed 2026-09-25; Alpaca partnership post https://alpaca.markets/blog/elevate-your-trading-with-the-new-alpaca-and-quantconnect-integration/). It is exposed through lean-cli: backtest --data-provider-historical Alpaca and --alpaca-environment [live|paper] (https://github.com/QuantConnect/lean-cli/blob/20e58aa65c3c504a6a585e1d4eb1b2e56b233c48/README.md lines 171, 243).

It has the deepest documented equity-data semantics when paired with QuantConnect's US Equity Security Master: January 1998 onward, about 27,500 US equities, with splits, dividends, mergers, IPOs and delistings (https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/datasets/quantconnect/us-equity-security-master).

Gates verified in source and docs:
- CLI use requires membership in 'an organization on a paid tier'. Locally the Alpaca provider serves raw data only; adjusted data needs the Security Master (https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/lean-cli/live-trading/brokerages/alpaca).
- Every Initialize/SetJob path calls ValidateSubscription() for product 347. It posts machine name, user name, domain, OS and NIC IP/MAC to modules/license/read and shuts down on failure (https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean.Brokerages.Alpaca/blob/e623e7963c6319455b9057a9c6f9c272e7453d37/QuantConnect.AlpacaBrokerage/AlpacaBrokerage.cs lines 179, 1421-1543; DataQueueHandler.cs line 81).
- The repo vendors a prebuilt Alpaca.Markets.dll and has no LICENSE file; the README declares Apache-2.0.
- In backtests, Alpaca-model orders get no slippage and market orders fill 'immediately and completely' (README lines 209-215 at the same commit).
ranked.versus_current: Better than Nautilus on packaged security-master semantics and upstream Alpaca support. Worse on cost (paid tier plus separately priced datasets), host-identity upload, a vendored binary and naive default fills. It keeps the frozen-oracle role (LEAN 985ef30). The Alpaca brokerage stays conditional, as blueprints/us-equities/engine/resolution-receipt.json already records ('Initialize calls ValidateSubscription').
ranked.trial:
Only if the user approves a QuantConnect paid-tier organization and the ValidateSubscription host-identity upload:
(1) lean backtest --data-provider-historical Alpaca over the spy-parity one_zero window, compared bar for bar with the retained alpaca-py SIP raw bars. Pass = 0 OHLCV mismatches.
(2) lean live deploy --brokerage Alpaca --alpaca-environment paper: one SPY long-to-flat round trip, with the in-repo engine stopped (one owned writer), scored on the alpaca-paper-smoke contract. Pass = filled, flat, cash reconciled, completed-trial recovery with 0 duplicate writes, and an independent alpaca-py observation that agrees.

ranked.name: alpaca-py 0.44.0 + in-repo Alpaca adapter (current Alpaca path)
ranked.why:
The official SDK. v0.44.0 (2026-08-11) is both the pin and the latest release (https://github.com/alpacahq/alpaca-py/releases/tag/v0.44.0). Bars offer raw/split/dividend/all adjustment, asof symbol mapping and the SIP feed, and corporate actions have their own endpoint (https://docs.alpaca.markets/reference/stockbars ; https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/reference/corporateactions-1).

It carries this repo's qualified paper lifecycle. alpaca-paper-smoke, adaptive-paper-broker-trial and native-fault-behaviour are established, and 180 order actions per minute over five windows ran with 0 HTTP 429 at the observed 200/min limit (catalogs/us-equities/gates-20260922.json; runtime-target.json).

Limits:
- History starts in 2016, there is no historical security type, and delisted coverage is unmeasured (blueprints/us-equities/alpaca-history-fixture/README.md).
- Paper trading does not simulate market impact, latency slippage, queue position or dividends, and 'when orders are eligible to be filled, they will receive partial fills for a random size 10%' of the time (https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/paper-trading, updated 2026-07-07).
ranked.versus_current: This is the current path. The Python alternatives reviewed wrap this same SDK: Lumibot (verified here at v4.6.1), plus ml4t-live, roboquant.py, Vibe-Trading, QuantDinger and AlpacaTradingAgent (per the pinned source in the GitHub return). None of them adds broker capability; they change simulation and data semantics only. The 10% random partial fills and missing impact apply to every Alpaca-paper route below.
ranked.trial:
Already frozen and waiting only for keys: alpaca-history-fixture-v1-20260925 (1,236 Form 25-NSE rows for 2016-2019, 235 collisions, LOGC/TEN/BTX/CBIO, 130 owed rows). Preregistered pass bars:
- pre-2020-delisting: at least 95% of rows each year with price paths that stop within 10 sessions of the filing
- dated-security-identity: unresolved_collisions == 0 (predicted to fail, because the API has no security type)

ranked.name: QuantRocket (Zipline + Moonshot, bundled US stock data)
ranked.why:
The only Alpaca-listed platform (https://alpaca.markets/integrations) that bundles survivorship-free history: 'Survivorship-bias-free 1-minute US stock data is included with the software, with history back to 2007' (https://www.quantrocket.com/alpaca). Its data library lists US Stock Prices from 2007 to present, end-of-day and 1-minute, delisted stocks included, split- and dividend-adjusted, vendor QuantRocket, 'included with software license' (https://www.quantrocket.com/data/). Its docs say 'You can connect to one or more paper Alpaca accounts and one or more live Alpaca accounts' (https://www.quantrocket.com/docs/). It is active: quantrocket-client tag 2.12.0.0 was committed 2026-09-16, newer than the 2.11 the GPT-6 return reported (https://github.com/quantrocket-llc/quantrocket-client/tags).

Blocking facts:
- The free plan has only sample data (2007-2011 US prices) and 'No live or paper trading' (https://www.quantrocket.com/pricing/).
- The docs say 'paper trading requires that the live account limit has previously been validated. Thus before paper trading it is first necessary to connect your live account at least once' (https://www.quantrocket.com/docs/). This repo's paper-only, no-live-key policy forbids that.
- It is proprietary. Zipline commissions and slippage are off by default and Moonshot is vectorized (QuantRocket docs as cited by two returns; not re-fetched here, the page was truncated).
ranked.versus_current: Better than alpaca-py/Alpaca history on depth (2007 vs 2016) and on explicit delisted coverage, which are exactly the two open gates, pre-2020-delisting and dated-security-identity. Worse than Nautilus on execution realism. Its Alpaca paper route is unusable here, so its value is a licensed data arm, not a platform switch. The catalog knows only moonshot, as 'IBKR-based' discovery.
ranked.trial:
Trigger: after the Alpaca fixture receipt, and only if an identity gate stays open and the user approves one month-to-month license. Load usstock daily/minute data and its securities master for 2016-2019 and score them with the unchanged alpaca-history-fixture-v1-20260925 fixtures and rules. Pass:
- at least 95% of the 1,236 delisting rows each year with price paths that stop within 10 sessions of the filing
- unresolved_collisions == 0 across the 235 collisions, with dated tenures and security type
- all four reused tickers pass
Research and backtest use only (the license account limit does not apply to historical data); no QuantRocket paper trading. An optional free pre-check is possible on the 2007-2011 sample bundle, but it cannot test the 2016-2019 gate years.

ranked.name: ml4t-backtest 0.1.12 + ml4t-live 0.1.2 + ml4t-data 0.2.0
ranked.why:
MIT; all three pushed 2026-09-24/25. They are written almost entirely by stefan-jansen, who also maintains zipline-reloaded: 178 commits on backtest (https://api.github.com/repos/ml4t/backtest/contributors).

ml4t-backtest is event-driven, with same-bar or next-bar fills and quote-aware execution. It ships a 'lean' preset: 'Match the frozen LEAN daily US-equity protocol (next-session open, integer shares)'. Its generated real-strategy audit reports 17/17 required pairs passing, including LEAN 18001 on a US equity panel with 'fills equal at declared field precision; 4,027 valuations within $0.01'; that protocol runs without costs (https://github.com/ml4t/backtest/blob/672804b36915742fe18af9cd09b44e9839d39d6f/README.md lines 145-157, 308-335).

ml4t-live runs strategies against IBKR or Alpaca with SafeBroker limits and a shadow-to-paper path. Its Alpaca execution adapter is 'stable-supported' while the Alpaca feed is experimental opt-in; state files are 0600; it supports Python 3.12-3.14 on Linux, macOS and Windows (https://github.com/ml4t/live/blob/43fc66f4a56a3861d4c3e05efcf3e9ab06be4461/README.md lines 7-15, 65-75).

Risks: created November 2025, pre-1.0, 22-50 stars, effectively one maintainer. There is no survivorship tooling, and dividend-cash handling is unverified.
ranked.versus_current: It could be a cheap, Python-native third engine for the daily-bar LEAN parity oracle, with volume-participation partial fills and market impact that Nautilus gets only by configuration. It has no order-book, queue or latency model, so it cannot replace Nautilus for intraday realism, and it is far less proven than LEAN or Nautilus. The catalog records only ml4t/backtest, as discovery_only.
ranked.trial:
Now, at no cost: replay the frozen spy-parity one_zero inputs with BacktestConfig.from_preset('lean'), through a thin runner that writes a compare.py-schema receipt. Score it with blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus/spy-parity/compare.py against the LEAN 985ef30 oracle (receipt sha256 06ec0656...).
Pass = PASS with every check inside tolerances.json, zero unattributed failures and zero unexplained cash residue (fills 323.58/291.69, dividends 428.64, end cash 90734.080).
Only after a PASS: one SPY long-to-flat round trip through ml4t-live's Alpaca adapter, with paper keys from the existing 0600 store and the in-repo engine stopped, scored on the alpaca-paper-smoke contract.

ranked.name: Lumibot 4.6.1 (Lumiwealth)
ranked.why:
The most Alpaca-native maintained open framework:
- a native Alpaca broker on alpaca-py TradingClient with a paper flag and PARTIALLY_FILLED events (https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/blob/v4.6.1/lumibot/brokers/alpaca.py lines 450-452, 1797-1805)
- AlpacaBacktesting on the user's own Alpaca history, which accepts only a paper account and only day or minute bars (https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/blob/v4.6.1/lumibot/backtesting/alpaca_backtesting.py lines 248, 335)
- Databento, ThetaData, Polygon and pandas sources
Alpaca's own 2026-07-23 tutorial uses it to go from backtest to paper (https://alpaca.markets/learn/how-i-use-ai-to-research-and-test-trading-ideas-with-alpaca). v4.6.1 was released 2026-09-26.

The license conflict the catalog holds it on is resolved: LICENSE, setup.py license='GPL-3.0' and PyPI 4.6.1 all say GPL-3.0 (https://pypi.org/pypi/lumibot/4.6.1/json).

Realism is weak:
- Orders 'fill at the open of the bar that starts at the current time'.
- Slippage is one absolute amount per order.
- There is no latency or volume model.
- AlpacaBacktesting offers only split-adjusted or fully adjusted prices; auto_adjust defaults to 'all' (line 1304).
- An explicit config stops three trading days early unless full_window=True (https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/blob/v4.6.1/docsrc/backtesting.alpaca.rst lines 51-55, 115-129).
ranked.versus_current: Better developer path than Nautilus plus the in-repo adapter: one strategy class runs from backtest to Alpaca paper. Worse on fill realism. Its adjusted-price default conflicts with the raw-bars-plus-separate-actions policy, and it is GPL-3.0 copyleft. It is the alternative the backtesting-engine overturn_protocol names.
ranked.trial:
Now, at no cost:
(a) Replay the frozen spy-parity one_zero inputs through Lumibot pandas backtesting, with raw bars and the frozen dividend events, scored by compare.py against the LEAN 985ef30 oracle. Pass = PASS inside tolerances.json, zero unattributed failures, zero unexplained cash residue.
(b) One SPY long-to-flat round trip via its Alpaca broker with PAPER=True, paper keys from the existing 0600 store and the in-repo engine stopped. Pass = the alpaca-paper-smoke contract (filled, flat, cash reconciled, 0 duplicate writes on recovery, independent alpaca-py observation agrees).
Adoption beyond that still needs the adaptive_practice overturning comparison.

ranked.name: Blueshift (QuantInsti)
ranked.why: A hosted-only engine and Alpaca partner (https://alpaca.markets/integrations); Alpaca paper is listed on a (c) 2021 docs page (https://blueshift.quantinsti.com/docs/concepts/). Its US data is minute-level from July 2008 for 'a liquidity filtered universe of top 1000 stocks and ETFs', recomputed quarterly. Backtests fill at as-traded prices, and 'Traded volumes per order are capped at 2% available volume at that bar' (https://blueshift.quantinsti.com/docs/datasets/). Delisting coverage is not documented; the survivorship-bias sentence on that page is about Crypto. Nothing is exportable.

ranked.trial: None. Reopen if a local engine or a delisted-inclusive export appears.

# Answer to the user's question

**No — NautilusTrader and LEAN are far from the only options.** Verified live against `gh api`, PyPI, and Alpaca's/QuantConnect's own docs (not just re-trusting the three returns), the real landscape for an Alpaca-paper, historical-E2E Python/Rust workflow is:

- **LEAN + Lean.Brokerages.Alpaca** — deepest *official* integration, but its Alpaca backtest defaults to zero slippage and full immediate fills unless you override the models, and its richest historical data (Security Master/AlgoSeek) lives in paid QuantConnect Cloud datasets.
- **Lumibot** — single codebase from backtest to Alpaca paper via one flag; confirmed **GPL-3.0 throughout** (see Finding 1 below — a "GPL vs MIT" discrepancy claimed in one return does not exist).
- **ml4t-data / ml4t-backtest / ml4t-live** — newest (Nov 2025) and, on the evidence, the most technically rigorous pure-Python stack: volume-participation partial fills, market impact, next-bar-open semantics, a frozen LEAN-parity preset, shadow→paper→live staging. MIT. But pre-1.0 with 22–50 GitHub stars — real, but unproven at scale.
- **QuantRocket** — proprietary, self-hosted, Docker on Linux/macOS; bundles a vendor claim of survivorship-bias-free 1-min US data since 2007; supports multiple paper *and* live Alpaca accounts natively.
- **Alpaca's own official agent layer** — `alpacahq/alpaca-mcp-server` (MIT, paper-by-default, very active), `alpaca-skills`, `alpaca/cli`. Not a backtester.
- **vectorbt / PyBroker** — Alpaca as a *data source only* (no paper/live path), and both are Apache-2.0-plus-Commons-Clause (not OSI open source).
- **NautilusTrader**: confirmed **zero** Alpaca code upstream. RFC #3374 has been open since 2026-01-01 (8 comments, still unresolved); PR #3375 was opened and closed *unmerged the same day* — maintainer cited lack of capacity. Getting Alpaca into Nautilus today means a custom/community adapter (like this repo's own).
- Alpaca's own **integrations directory lists exactly 17 partners** (confirmed live, 2026-09-26): Alexa, AlgoBulls, Algorum, Arcade Trader, Blueshift, Breaking Equity, Composer, Passiv, PredictNow.ai, QuantRocket, Slack, Streak, Tradetron, TradingView, Trellis, Wealth-Lab, Zapier. That's the actual "full landscape" of *official* integrations; beyond it sits a long tail of independent OSS frameworks with their own Alpaca connectors (Lumibot, ml4t, vectorbt, PyBroker, roboquant, backtrader's now-frozen bridge, pylivetrader, FinRL, and several AI-agent frameworks).
- Your pinned `alpaca-py==0.44.0` is confirmed current — it is the actual latest release (2026-08-11).

**Tavily key:** not used. The string pasted in the request is a live-looking API key. Per this repo's `docs/secret-storage.md` and the standing rule to never read/print/copy a credential value, I did not paste it into any command. It wasn't needed either — `gh api` + official docs covered every check below. Recommend rotating it at the provider and storing the replacement as a 0600 per-provider file outside any worktree.

# Facts-refuter results (role requested by the workflow)

**Method:** pulled live GitHub metadata (license, stars, `pushed_at`, archived, default branch) and latest-release tag/date for all **44** distinct repos named across the three returns; cross-checked PyPI JSON wherever GitHub Releases were silent or a discrepancy was alleged; re-fetched cited files/line-ranges and re-ran `gh api search/code` for every "0 hits" exclusion claim; fetched Alpaca's and QuantConnect's live docs directly (`docs.alpaca.markets`, `alpaca.markets/integrations`, `quantrocket.com`, `wealth-lab.com`). ~100 `gh api` calls + ~10 PyPI/doc fetches, all live on 2026-09-26.

## Confirmed false / misleading

**1. [gpt6 blob] Lumibot license — FALSE.**
Claimed: *"current dev LICENSE is GPL-3.0, while inspected PyPI metadata says MIT... The v4.6.1 artifact license could not be fetched."*
Fact: I fetched it. PyPI JSON for `lumibot` **4.6.1** (the exact version in question) reports `license: "GPL-3.0"` with classifier `License :: OSI Approved :: GNU General Public License v3 (GPLv3)`, uploaded 2026‑09‑26T01:07:45Z. The `dev`-branch `LICENSE` file is literal GPLv3 text; GitHub's SPDX detection also says GPL-3.0. No MIT appears anywhere in current metadata — the claimed discrepancy doesn't exist.
Evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/lumibot/json · https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/blob/dev/LICENSE

**2. [official blob] QuantRocket client "Active" via tag 2.12.0.0 — misleading, not false.**
Claimed: *"Active: client tag 2.12.0.0 committed 2026-09-16... The client has 32 stars."*
Fact: the tag and date are real (commit `add411b1`, 2026‑09‑16T20:14:08Z, "fix for requests 2.34.x") — but it sits on a separate `2.12dev` branch. The repo's actual **default branch** (`master`, what a plain clone/`pip install` checks out) hasn't moved since **2024‑11‑06T14:46:38Z** — 22 months stale as of this check. "Active" is true only for the unmerged dev branch.
Evidence: https://github.com/quantrocket-llc/quantrocket-client/commits/master · https://github.com/quantrocket-llc/quantrocket-client/branches

That is the complete list of confirmed errors. Everything else specific and checkable that I tested held up — including several places the three returns *appear* to disagree with each other.

## Apparent disagreements that are not errors (different valid sources)
- **zipline-reloaded 3.1.1 date**: official/github say 2025‑07‑23 (GitHub Release `published_at` — confirmed); gpt6 says 2025‑07‑19 (PyPI `upload_time` — also confirmed; PyPI got the wheel 4 days before the GitHub Release was published).

- **hftbacktest "Python 2.4.4 / 2025-12-10"**: confirmed as the real current PyPI version — even though GitHub's own Release list tops out at `py-v2.1.1` (2024‑11‑24) for Python; 2025‑12‑10 is when the *Rust* crate (`rust-v0.9.4`) was tagged. Python and Rust release independently in this repo.

The `pushed_at` value used by official/github (2024‑08‑19) reflects a push to a *different* branch; master itself hasn't moved since April 2023. (Bonus: gpt6's "GPL-3.0-**or-later**" is also the more precise SPDX id — the LICENSE text literally contains "or any later version," which GitHub's own generic "GPL-3.0" tag elides.)
- **alpaca-backtrader-api "dormant since 2022-01-02"**: confirmed true by direct commit inspection — master's HEAD really is `475bb54b`, 2022‑01‑02. `pushed_at` shows 2026‑06‑23, but that's a push to a non-default branch (the repo has a dozen `pyup-scheduled-update-*`/`dependabot` branches), not master.
- **QuantRocket platform "2.11.0 (2025-01-28)"**: confirmed directly on QuantRocket's own changelog as the real latest platform release. The separate `quantrocket-client` GitHub package uses an independent version series (now 2.12.0.0) — the two numbers are for different components, not a contradiction.

## Central, decision-critical claims independently re-confirmed
- NautilusTrader `develop`: 18 adapter crates, **no Alpaca** (directory listing matches exactly); code search for "alpaca" = 0 hits. Issue #3374 open since 2026‑01‑01 (8 comments); PR #3375 opened/closed unmerged the same day. LGPL-3.0; v1.231.0 stable (2026‑08‑02); v2.0.0rc5 prerelease (2026‑09‑15) — exact matches. Its `FillModel`/`ProbabilisticFillState`/`LatencyModel` code citations check out at the exact cited line numbers.
- Lean.Brokerages.Alpaca: no LICENSE file (confirmed null), 18 stars, created 2024‑06‑07. README's exact lines: "Orders through Alpaca do not experience slippage in backtests" / "We fill market orders immediately and completely in backtests" and the required QC Security-Master/AlgoSeek/Coarse-Universe datasets — verbatim matches.
- LEAN: Apache-2.0, 21,781 stars, and its only-ever GitHub Release genuinely is v2.4.0.1 from 2017‑08‑08 (ships continuously off master since).

official.notes:
Scope: only the official Alpaca ecosystem, researched 2026-09-26 UTC.

Direct answer: No, NautilusTrader and LEAN are not the only options. Alpaca's integrations page (https://alpaca.markets/integrations) lists 17 partners, and its Learn articles and blog document more. Judged on merit for the north star (end-to-end historical US-equities simulation, then Alpaca paper, on Linux and macOS, maintained code), three stand out:
1. QuantConnect LEAN + Lean.Brokerages.Alpaca. The deepest official integration, and AlpacaBrokerageModel encodes Alpaca's order-type, fee and extended-hours rules. Its best historical data lives in QC Cloud.
2. QuantRocket. The only self-hosted platform here that bundles historical data (vendor claim: survivorship-bias-free 1-minute US data from 2007). It supports several paper and live Alpaca accounts and runs in Docker on Linux and macOS. It is proprietary and licensed against an account limit.
3. Lumibot. A maintained open-source route with Alpaca-data backtests (including options) and Alpaca paper through one flag, featured by Alpaca in July 2026. It is GPL-3.0, fills at the bar open, and documents no survivorship or corporate-action pipeline.

The rest fit less well:
- Blueshift is closed and cloud-only.
- vectorbt is a data-only research library under the Commons Clause.
- The Backtrader adapter, pylivetrader and LiuAlgoTrader have been dormant since 2022-2023.
- WealthLab runs only on Windows.
- Composer, Tradetron, AlgoBulls and TradingView offered no reproducible local historical pipeline in the sources retrieved.
- Alpaca's own backtesting content from 2024-2026 uses hand-written alpaca-py code and AI workflows (MCP server, Lumibot), not a named engine.

NautilusTrader: none of the Alpaca listings found include it, and upstream has no Alpaca adapter. crates/adapters on the develop branch contains architect_ax, betfair, binance, blockchain, bybit, coinbase, databento, deribit, derive, dydx, hyperliquid, interactive_brokers, kraken, lighter, okx, polymarket, sandbox and tardis (https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/adapters). GitHub code search for 'alpaca' in the repo returned 0 hits (default-branch index). This matches the runtime target's custom Python Alpaca adapter.

Alpaca paper rules apply to every paper route above (https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/paper-trading.md, updatedAt 2026-07-07):
- Not simulated: dividends, market impact, information leakage, slippage from latency, queue position, price improvement and regulatory fees. Borrow fees are marked 'coming soon'.
- Orders fill only once they are marketable.
- Order size is not checked against NBBO size.
- Partial fills of a random size happen 10% of the time.
No platform in this set documents latency or queue-position modelling in backtests.

License and supply-chain flags:
- GitHub detects no license in Lean.Brokerages.Alpaca.
- vectorbt is Apache-2.0 plus the Commons Clause.
- Lumibot and Backtrader are GPL-3.0.
- QuantRocket, Blueshift, WealthLab, TradingView, Composer, Tradetron and the AlgoBulls platform are proprietary.

Evidence level: review of documentation, blog posts and GitHub metadata only. No platform was installed or run, and no performance was measured. Items tagged '(search snippet)' come from search-result summaries, not direct fetches, and need a fetch before being cited as accepted. Budget used: 15/15 web searches, 15/15 fetches and 40/40 gh api calls, plus local reads of the catalog and runtime target on origin/main and one read of installed wheel metadata. Existing catalog dispositions for Lumibot, vectorbt, Backtrader, Zipline and the LEAN Alpaca brokerage were not changed.

github.notes:
Short answer: no, NautilusTrader and LEAN are not the only options. The code check found these Alpaca paths:
- LEAN has an official Alpaca plugin.
- NautilusTrader has no upstream Alpaca adapter.
- Lumibot is the most Alpaca-native end-to-end framework.
- The ML4T libraries (ml4t-data, ml4t-backtest, ml4t-live) are a new MIT stack with the strongest Python execution realism.
- vectorbt and PyBroker use Alpaca for data only, under Commons Clause.
- roboquant (Python and Kotlin) and FinRL-X also connect to Alpaca.
- Agent layers: the official alpaca-mcp-server, Vibe-Trading, QuantDinger and AlpacaTradingAgent.
- backtrader's Alpaca bridge is legacy.

Stars are context only.

**Assessment against the north star (judgement, not measured):**
- NautilusTrader: no engine checked here has stronger verified simulation building blocks (fill and latency models). But Alpaca support needs a custom or community adapter; the maintainer declined PR #3375 for capacity reasons, and RFC #3374 is open.
- LEAN: the only engine with a maintained, official Alpaca brokerage, live data and historical provider. `lean data download` / `lean backtest --data-provider-historical Alpaca` works end to end. Its documented Alpaca backtest defaults are no slippage and full immediate fills, and corporate actions and universes come from QuantConnect datasets.
- Best candidates for the runtime-target's overturn comparison (same frozen data and risk contract):
  - Lumibot: same code from backtest to Alpaca paper; used in Alpaca's own 2026-07-23 article; GPL-3.0. Weaknesses: absolute-amount slippage only, and AlpacaBacktesting supports day or minute bars only.
  - ml4t-backtest/ml4t-live: volume-participation partial fills, market impact, next-bar-open semantics, parity presets including a LEAN protocol, shadow-to-paper-to-live staging. Weakness: pre-1.0 with low adoption.
- vectorbt and PyBroker: research accelerators only (no paper path).
- None of the Alpaca-native frameworks showed survivorship-free universe or delisting handling in code.

**Alpaca-side facts:**
- The historical bars endpoint (https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/reference/stockbars) offers:
  - adjustment: raw, split, dividend, spin-off or all; default raw.
  - asof: default is the current day; used to link symbol renames.
  - feed: iex, otc, sip or boats; default sip.
- The FAQ (https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/market-data-faq) says SIP historical queries need end at least 15 minutes old without a subscription. It does not document history depth or delisted-symbol coverage, so survivorship-free universes need another source (for example QuantConnect's security master in LEAN).
- Corporate actions have their own endpoint (https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/reference/corporateactions-1).
- Alpaca's integrations page (https://alpaca.markets/integrations) lists only commercial or hosted platforms: TradingView, Streak, QuantRocket, Blueshift, Tradetron, Arcade Trader, AlgoBulls, Trellis, Breaking Equity, Composer, Algorum, Wealth-Lab, Passiv, PredictNow.ai, Slack, Zapier and Alexa. None were evaluated in code.
- Alpaca's official agent tooling is alpaca-mcp-server v2, alpaca-skills, the Alpaca CLI and alpacahq/agentic.

**Checked and excluded:**
- StockSharp (10,802 stars): the README lists Alpaca, but StockSharp.slnx references ../Connectors/Alpaca/Alpaca.csproj, which is outside the public repository (the public tree only has an Alpaca logo), so it cannot be verified.
- rburkholder/trade-frame (C++): has lib/TFAlpaca for real-time data and orders, but LICENSE.txt says it 'may not be used nor distributed without proper license agreement'.
- Code search for 'alpaca' returned total_count 0 in stefan-jansen/zipline-reloaded (last commit 2025-11-13), microsoft/qlib, nkaz001/hftbacktest (the sim cross-check; last push 2025-12-23), barter-rs/barter-rs, coding-kitties/investing-algorithm-framework and TauricResearch/TradingAgents.
- Stale by metadata: blankly (last push 2024-12-30, latest release v1.18.0-beta from 2022), LiuAlgoTrader (2023-08-13), alpacahq/alpaca-zipline (2022-10-23).
- Broad code search: alpaca-py TradingClient in brokers/ paths hit 21 files across 20 small personal repos; the deprecated SDK hit 10. Neither surfaced a framework-grade engine.
- tradermonty/claude-trading-skills (2,889 stars) uses Alpaca MCP and adapters (87 code hits); it is an agent-skills collection, not an engine.

**Method and evidence class:**
- Evidence is metadata plus pinned source review only. Nothing was installed, run natively, or paper-traded. Performance and portability were not benchmarked; verified OS support is limited to ml4t-live (Linux, macOS, Windows) and LEAN via Docker images.
- Budgets used: 56 of 60 gh api calls, 3 of 10 web searches, 7 of 10 fetches.
- Default-branch heads were rechecked unchanged before citing README line numbers.
- Supply-chain points (archived SDK use in FinRL and backtrader, the vendored Alpaca.Markets.dll in the LEAN plugin, Commons Clause, copyleft) were checked by hand; the supply-chain-risk-auditor skill was not run.
- The pasted Tavily key was not used or copied into any command, per AGENTS.md and docs/secret-storage.md. It appeared in plain text in the request, so rotating it and storing it as a 0600 provider file is advisable if Tavily is wanted.
- Raw API outputs are local scratch, not evidence of record: <scratch> (meta.json, tree_*.json, blobs/, calls.log).

platforms.name: LumiBot
platforms.kind: Integrated Python research, backtesting and broker framework. OS-independent packaging and maintainer macOS/M3 acceptance records support portability investigation; neither supplied host was tested. [Package](https://pypi.org/project/lumibot/), [Acceptance records](https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/blob/dev/docs/ACCEPTANCE_BACKTESTS.md).
platforms.alpaca_support: Native Alpaca broker; current implementation uses alpaca-py and exposes paper configuration. [Broker documentation](https://lumibot.lumiwealth.com/brokers.alpaca.html), [Implementation](https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/blob/dev/lumibot/brokers/alpaca.py).
platforms.historical_data_e2e: Alpaca historical download/cache/backtest path exists alongside other providers. Corporate-action handling is provider-specific; a complete historical universe, delisted coverage and point-in-time membership are not established for its Alpaca path. [Alpaca backtesting](https://lumibot.lumiwealth.com/backtesting.alpaca.html), [Architecture](https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/blob/dev/docs/BACKTESTING_ARCHITECTURE.md).
platforms.backtest_realism: Bar-based execution and configurable slippage. Historical queue, latency and volume-constrained partial-fill fidelity remain unverified. Current docs default to completed history bars; disabling remove_incomplete_current_bar introduces lookahead. Explicit configuration still needs full_window=True to avoid ending three trading sessions early. [Backtesting semantics](https://lumibot.lumiwealth.com/backtesting.alpaca.html), [Slippage](https://lumibot.lumiwealth.com/entities.trading_slippage.html).
platforms.paper_path: Run the strategy with the native Alpaca broker and PAPER=True. Documented integration merits independent paper qualification; it is not qualification evidence itself. [Paper configuration](https://lumibot.lumiwealth.com/brokers.alpaca.html).
platforms.license: Unresolved version-specific discrepancy: current dev LICENSE is GPL-3.0, while inspected PyPI metadata says MIT. The v4.6.1 artifact license could not be fetched. [Repository license](https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/blob/dev/LICENSE), [Package metadata](https://pypi.org/project/lumibot/).
platforms.maintenance: Recent releases include Alpaca backtest configuration fixes and IBKR fill/dividend fixes. Recheck behavior against the exact installed version because documentation and package metadata differ. [Releases](https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/releases).
evidence: Release/date: [Release listing](https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/releases), [v4.6.1 change](https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot/pull/1180).
Assessment: a prominent additional Python-to-Alpaca candidate; historical-universe coverage, simulation fixtures and artifact licensing remain adoption gates.

platforms.historical_data_e2e: Databento historical/DBN ingestion and catalog storage are documented. platforms.paper_path: Documented IBKR paper connection or internal sandbox; an Alpaca paper path needs its own adapter/integration qualification. [IBKR paper](https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/integrations/interactive_brokers/), [Integration inventory](https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/integrations/).

evidence: Release/date: [Official releases](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/releases).

evidence: Assessment: useful specialist cross-check on execution assumptions; not a complete Alpaca US-equities platform.

The supplied Elite account's higher limits do not establish different simulation semantics. [Paper specification](https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/paper-trading). Paper qualification should therefore assess operational behavior independently of historical performance.
